readerFieldReview.finding: The author removed internal editorial wording and aligned the display name to WEB Shemariah. The base says he is listed among Rehoboam’s sons alongside Jeush and Zaham. No later assigned-book facts or future same-name comparisons are present in current reader fields.
readerFieldReview.contextCheck: WEB 2CH 11:18 names Rehoboam taking Mahalath as wife; 11:19 then says she bore him sons and names Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham. Thus Rehoboam is the immediate context for “him”; the profile knownBy remains at the named occurrence 11:19.

wikipediaReview.locator: Shemariah section, lines 1524–1530, especially line 1528. The list says there are four biblical figures named Shemariah; its 2 Chronicles 11:19 entry is a son of Rehoboam and spells the name Shamariah in the KJV.
wikipediaReview.assessment: The candidate label Shamariah corresponds to the same 2CH 11:19 entry, not a different person inferred from similar spelling. identityVerified=true is supported for this translation-variant mapping. The note accurately identifies the KJV as the named spelling source. Wikipedia is secondary evidence, not a claim made in WEB itself.
